# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination

**RE: Appeal of Denial – Total Shoulder Replacement (CPT 23472)**
**Member:** Reese Carter
**Member ID:** W451155739
**Plan:** Iowa Total Care (Commercial/ACA)
**Denial date:** 2026-08-18
**Reference number:** POC-EF30A43966-84895
**Governing policy cited:** 2026 Evolent MSK Surgery Guidelines (https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2026-05/2026%20Evolent%20Musculoskeletal%20Surgery%20Guidelines.pdf), effective 2026-07-01

Dear Iowa Total Care Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my total shoulder replacement (CPT 23472), which was denied on 2026-08-18 under reference number POC-EF30A43966-84895. My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I am asking the plan to reconsider its decision.

## Why I am appealing

The denial letter states that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I want to walk through what conservative treatment I actually completed, because I believe the record shows otherwise.

**A note on the policy criteria:** The specific criteria language provided to me in connection with this denial is drawn from the cervical spine fusion sections of the 2026 Evolent MSK Surgery Guidelines (covering ACDF, cervical posterior decompression with fusion, and cervical fusion for axial neck pain). None of that language addresses shoulder replacement, and I have not been given the specific criteria the plan applied to a total shoulder replacement request. I am not able to quote plan language that does not pertain to my procedure, so I am setting out below, in my own words, why my treatment history should satisfy any reasonable conservative-care requirement for this surgery. I am also formally requesting, below, that the plan provide me the actual criteria it applied to CPT 23472.

## My treatment history

Before surgery was recommended, I completed the following conservative treatment for my shoulder condition over approximately 12 months:

- **Physical therapy:** 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics, from 2026-04-13 to 2026-07-20, with 18 visits completed. This is documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication:** NSAIDs for 4 months, which did not adequately relieve my symptoms.
- **Injection:** A corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-27, which gave only about 3 weeks of partial relief before my symptoms returned.
- **Imaging:** An MRI of my shoulder on 2026-07-07 showed a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm with grade 2 fatty atrophy.
- **Ongoing impact:** I cannot lift my arm above shoulder height or sleep on the affected side. On examination, I have positive provocative testing on the affected side, and my range of motion is limited by pain.

I have no active infection and no untreated substance use, and I do not smoke, which I understand can be relevant to surgical candidacy.

I completed physical therapy, tried medication, and tried an injection, none of which resolved my symptoms, and my MRI confirms a significant structural injury (a full-thickness tear with fatty atrophy) that is unlikely to improve with further non-surgical care. I believe this record reflects a genuine trial of conservative treatment that did not succeed, not a lack of effort or documentation.

## Request that the plan provide the criteria it applied

I understand that Iowa Total Care routes musculoskeletal surgical authorization decisions, including shoulder procedures, to Evolent, and that Evolent's clinical criteria are published on RadMD. I am requesting that the plan confirm whether this request was reviewed under Evolent's criteria and, if so, provide me in writing the specific criteria section applicable to total shoulder replacement (CPT 23472) that was used to issue this denial, including the conservative-care requirements referenced. I am entitled to know the actual standard being applied to my case, and I cannot fully respond to the denial without it.

## What I am asking for

I am asking Iowa Total Care to reconsider and overturn the denial of my total shoulder replacement, based on the conservative treatment history documented above and my surgeon's determination that surgery is now medically necessary. If the plan intends to maintain the denial, I ask that it identify the specific shoulder-replacement criteria in the 2026 Evolent MSK Surgery Guidelines that it believes my records do not meet.

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-14, and I am submitting it through the appeal process described in my denial letter. I also understand appeals may be submitted online at ambetterhealth.com (selecting Iowa and the appeal/grievance form) or by calling the number on my member ID card, and that mail should go to the address printed on my denial letter.

Thank you for reconsidering my request. Please contact me if you need any additional information from me or my surgeon's office.

Sincerely,

[Reese Carter's signature]
Reese Carter
Member ID: W451155739
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
Date: [Date]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*

quotes: Cervical Fusion for Treatment of Axial Neck Pain Criteria Anterior Cervical Discectomy with Fusion (ACDF) – Multiple Levels When one of the two following criteria are met (1–8):

○ Upper extremity weakness ○ Unsteady gait related to myelopathy/balance or generalized lower extremity weakness ○ Disturbance with coordination ○ Hyperreflexia ○ Hoffmann sign ○ Positive Babinski sign and/or clonus ● Progressive neurological deficit (motor deficit, bowel or bladder dysfunction) with corresponding evidence of spinal cord or nerve root compression on an MRI or CT scan images – immediate surgical evaluation is indicated When ALL of the following criteria are met (6–8):

● Cervical radiculopathy or myelopathy due to ruptured disc, spondylosis, spinal instability, or deformity ● Failure of conservative treatment* for a minimum of six (6) weeks within the last six (6) months;
See Cervical Fusion for Treatment of Axial Neck Pain Criteria Cervical Posterior Decompression with Fusion (CPDF) - Single Level When one of the two following criteria are met (1–8,11):

● Cervical radiculopathy or myelopathy from ruptured disc, spondylosis, spinal instability, or deformity OR documented pseudarthrosis of prior ACDF/Cervical Artificial Disc Replacement (CADR) - one of the most common indications for a Single Level or Multi Levels CPDF is a failed anterior procedure ● Failure of conservative treatment* for a minimum of six (6) weeks within the last six (6) months;
NOTE - Failure of conservative treatment is defined as one of the following:

OR ○ Documentation of a medical reason the member is unable to participate in treatment Closure of medical or therapy offices, patient inconvenience, or noncompliance without explanation does not constitute “inability to complete” treatment.

See Cervical Fusion for Treatment of Axial Neck Pain Criteria Cervical Fusion for Treatment of Axial Neck Pain Fusion In Individuals with Non-Radicular Cervical Pain ALL of the following criteria must be met (14,15):

● Improvement of the symptoms has failed or plateaued, and the residual symptoms of pain and functional disability are unacceptable at the end of 6 to 12 consecutive months of appropriate, active treatment, or at the end of longer duration of non- operative programs for those debilitated with complex problems NOTE:
● Cervical radiculopathy from ruptured disc, spondylosis, or deformity ● Failure of conservative treatment* for a minimum of six (6) weeks within the last six (6) months;

preferred for examining bony structures, or in individuals presenting with clinical symptoms or signs inconsistent with MRI findings (e.g., foraminal compression not seen on MRI) As first-line treatment without conservative care measures in the following clinical cases (1,2,6,9):
